API versions: 62.0 and 67.0 (tooling REST and test classes at matching source versions).
Routes: executeAnonymous and isolated @IsTest with fixed IDs. Query rows use Search.query. The find and inline rows use Search.find/getSObject and inline SOSL respectively.
All data are synthetic. Fresh 30-day Developer scratch orgs. Anonymous setup committed in a separate transaction. Each @IsTest class seeded its own data, set fixed IDs, and transported observations via intentional assertion failure. Every test method had to transport the expected marker and full set of outcomes.
The small population is five Accounts (A–E), three Contacts (K–M) and two Leads (X,Y). Before accepting indexed outcomes, the driver required all three ordered label lists exactly twice in consecutive transactions at each API. Both versions passed on attempts 1 and 2. The first @IsTest column uses fixed IDs in L D X B K E M Y C A order. The second uses B M Y C K D X E L A. Anonymous repeats use independently executed queries over the same committed population. Rows with a dash in the repeat column were observed once per API/route. Entry-point twins used alphabetical descending fixed IDs per object, all queries explicitly ordered their groups.
Small fixture: use seed.apex, WindowSample.observe with a batch of up to ten rows from queries.tsv, and index-ready.apex. Inline rows replace the curly-braced term with an Apex literal. Search.find rows read .get(object), then getSObject().get(field). Test setup uses WindowSample.seed().
Large fixture: 2,002 Accounts and two Contacts. The driver verified each half in a separate single-object search (1,000 and 1,002 records, ordered endpoints 0000..0999 and 1000..2001) and both Contact endpoints K,M in two consecutive transactions per API. Queries use LargeSearchWindow.summary and large-seed.apex. The named route uses all fixture IDs as fixed results. Outputs here are [count:first label:last label] in RETURNING order. In anonymous multi-entity queries, the large indexed population yielded differing endpoints on repeats, including 0200..0449 and 1200..2001. Only cardinality is asserted there. Smaller anonymous groups with no explicit order also assert cardinality only. The raw identity observations remain in org.tsv.
Capture comparison: full native exception type/message for rejected queries, group membership and order for small explicitly ordered/fixed results. Record identities are normalized using seeded labels. A dash means no second repetition on that route.
Scratch cleanup: confirmed deletion after capture.
Queries: 254. Nonempty observed cells: 1528.
